Kameda was a king who won a political and ideological struggle against Umio, who was not a monarch. Umio was assassinated by agents acting for Kameda’s faction. Afterward, that faction arranged for Umio to be buried secretly and dishonorably. Kameda, by contrast, was cremated after his death as part of his ordinary funeral rites, leaving his remains fragmented. So the contrast in their bodies did not indicate who had won: Umio’s intact body concealed the ignominy of his burial, while Kameda’s fragments were simply the result of cremation.
